newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Montedison returns to dividend payments.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Montedison returns to dividend payments.

text.p: Italian agro-industry and chemicals group Montedison on Tuesday returned to paying its shareholders a dividend as it reported the first underlying net profit since a near-crippling 1993 financial crisis.
The group said it would pay out a dividend of 20 lire on each ordinary shares and 150 lire on its savings shares for 1996.
The payouts provided a further sign of its return to health since almost collapsing under a mountain of debt some four years ago.

Montedison reported a consolidated net profit of 298 billion lire ($175 million) for 1996 which compares with a net profit of 1.070 trillion in 1995 -- but this was boosted by a one-off gain of 1.135 trillion from the setting up of its Montell venture.

Montedison and its sister company Ferruzzi Finanziaria, now called Compart, went to the brink of financial ruin in 1993 when massive debts were uncovered, and neither company has paid a dividend since. The payout will be made on July 21 and will cost Montedison some 210 billion lire.
In a further sign of improvement, the group's consolidated net debt at end-1996 fell by 15.4 percent, or 1.514 trillion lire, to 8.324 trillion lire compared to end-1995 levels.

Progress continued in the first quarter of 1997 with group sales up 7.2 percent from first quarter 1996, while gross operating margins were around 60 billion lire higher, largely due to improvements in its energy and polymers interests.
Overall operating margins rose slightly to 13.4 percent from 13.3 percent from the first quarter of 1996.

Of Montedison's four main operating areas only energy, where the group has a controlling stake in energy producing group Edison, saw a rise in profits. Energy more than doubled operating profits to 661 billion lire in 1996.

Montedison's agro-industry interests, accounted for by its 50.4 percent holding in Paris-quoted Eridania Begin-Say, and chemicals, which includes its Montell polypropylene joint venture with oil group Shell, saw profits fall. Engineering profits were steady.

For the whole of 1996, operating profits rose 3.7 percent to 1.982 trillion lire while group sales fell by 0.9 percent to 23.959 trillion lire, reflecting the strength of the lira and the group's policy to re-focus and sell off non-core interests.
At the parent company level, Montedison SpA 1996 net profits rose 30.4 percent to 330 billion lire.
Compart, which holds a 31 percent stake in Montedison, said its 1996 net profits rose to 96 billion lire from 11 billion lire in 1995, but there was no return to dividend payments.

On when the group plans a return to dividend payments chairman Luigi Lucchini said, "I do not know, but there is optimism from the group's figures in the first months of 1997 and there is a continuing trend of improvement." ($1=1,708 lire)
